model: ADR 170 multi-task distributional model, extended by ADR 175

architecture.trunk: Linear(d_in,384) GELU Dropout -> Linear(384,384) GELU Dropout -> Linear(384,192) GELU
architecture.params_note: Trunk unchanged from ADR 170; the delta is exactly the two heads ADR 175 added, at 6176 parameters each. The absolute count depends on d_in, which depends on the one-hot width of sector and signal_type and therefore on the data.

ensemble: mean of per-seed pmfs, then invert (NOT mean of quantiles)
selection: median best-step across the purged walk-forward ladder at horizon_days=10, then refit on all of train

removed.breach_depth: ADR 177, 2026-09-08. Read the signal day's LOW against the t-1 band -- known to a `next_open` entry, not to a `touch` entry, so look-ahead once the convention changed (invariant 3). Worth 0.0003 AUC where it was legal.

measured_on_validate.applies_to: the 4-head ADR 170 model, before ADR 173 and ADR 175. Retained as the record of what ADR 172's holdout run scored, not as a claim about the current architecture.

gate: FAILS DESIGN 7.7 check 3 (coverage 17/20, needs 20/20). NOT promoted.
known_limitation: Calibrated for uptrending and choppy markets. All three coverage failures are 2022, the only sustained decline in train+validate. Train is 90.9% uptrend by index-above-200SMA; validate is 58.8%.
revision_notes: ADR 177 moved training and serving to `touch` entry (same-bar fill at the signal price) from `next_open`. With population held constant, p_touch_3 Brier skill +6.57% -> +10.14% and p_adverse_3 +3.83% -> +7.17%. `breach_depth` deleted in the same change as look-ahead under that convention. Stochastic-only signals leave the population entirely (no band level to fill at); confluence retains the stochastic condition because DESIGN 4.7's debounce already folds coincident rows into it. ADR 175 added the adverse family: heads went from 4 to 6 with ('trough', 5) and ('trough', 10), reading the new events.trough_ret_{h}d columns. Those are the exact mirror of peak_ret_* computed from path.adverse, NOT events.mae -- mae is adverse excursion until the trade exits, so ExitParams would be baked into the target and every sweep of stop_atr_k would silently redefine it. Earlier, ADR 173 added signal_type as a categorical (the model was never told whether a signal is a long or a short). EVERY measured_on_validate and holdout figure below predates BOTH changes and the seeding fix: they describe the 4-head model listed as previous_tasks, not the model this file now specifies.
reproducibility_warning: Every figure here was measured before 2026-09-04, when `_run` built the module BEFORE calling torch.manual_seed -- so initial weights were unseeded and the seeds controlled only the batch shuffle. Two runs of identical code gave step counts [364, 384, 372] and [437, 323, 510], and validate coverage 17/20 and 14/20. Seeding order is fixed and cuDNN pinned as of that date; these numbers have NOT been re-measured under the fix.

holdout.applies_to: the 4-head ADR 170 model, before ADR 173 and ADR 175. Retained as the record of what ADR 172's holdout run scored, not as a claim about the current architecture.

calibration_adr174.method: equal-mass buckets, isotonic (PAVA) pooling, Wilson interval on Kish n_eff
calibration_adr174.interval_source: the realised rate of past predictions in the same reliability bucket, NOT the ensemble seed spread, which measures the optimiser rather than the world
calibration_adr174.caveat: fitted on a split reused during model selection, so the interval is a lower bound on the true uncertainty
